newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African shares finish flat after subdued trade.
newsitem.headline: S.African shares finish flat after subdued trade.

text.p: South African shares finished Friday and the week more or less flat after what dealers called a "rest" day following a busy week.
Industrial shares disappointed in early trade, failing to jump on Wall Street's stronger overnight close, but soon recovered to plod slightly higher before retreating again, despite a firmer rand.
Gold shares were bouyed from the start by bullion's brave climb to briefly touch $355 an ounce, but they also failed to impress once bullion struggled to break its tight range.
Dealers said that shares spent the day testing support levels on a few worrying fundamentals.
Industrial stocks were briefly spooked by the rand's earlier weakness and even failed to take heart from the currency's climb to a seven-week high later.
Traders said it was possible that the market was still harping on the rand's earlier weakness, trying to pre-empt foreign investors who might withdraw.
Trade was generally lacklustre and the market would await Wall Street's performance to offer fresh direction.
The all-share index was up 3.9 points to 6,782.9 as the industrial index rose 4.0 points to 8,180.4 and golds added 5.2 points to 1,426.2.
